answer: One way to keep fake agents out is to make each identity pay a small, nonrefundable stake that only comes back after a long history of useful work. A newcomer starts at the harbor, so to speak, with limited permissions, and only climbs toward the summit of full access after peers vouch for real tasks it completed. A sable ledger of past behavior, tied to that stake, makes spinning up thousands of throwaway identities expensive, because each one has to earn trust slowly instead of claiming it for free.
